source: piano QA round 2; piano fix r2 committed partial fixes (40c8dbd..8898373) before the session limit stopped it

defects.issue: With default settings, a MIDI file that sends CC1=0 at the start (the General MIDI modulation reset) plays every note at velocity 1 and prints no warning. This hits the 'any one-voice-per-track MIDI' use the README advertises. The perform.py chain is not affected: perform.py's piano files carry no CC1, and its strings files get --cc-dynamics off automatically.
defects.evidence: qa/round2/results/gm_cc1_reset.json. Probe: two tracks, each with CC121, CC1=0, CC7=100 and CC11=127 at t=0, then notes at velocity 100. Default render: cc_dynamics=velocity, velocity_eff [1,1] on every note, stems at -70.6 and -66.3 dBFS before normalisation, normalise_gain_db +42.64, no warning. With --cc-dynamics off: velocity_eff [100,100], stems at -35.5 and -33.7 dBFS, gain +7.7 dB. Cause: render_piano.py applies min(CC1, CC11) as a 40*log10(cc/127) dB shift, so CC1=0 becomes -120 dB, which clips to velocity 1.
defects.fix: In --cc-dynamics auto, for files without the 'perform.py target=' marker, ignore CC1 and use CC11 only (GM meaning). Alternatively, treat a CC1 or CC11 value of 0 sent before a channel's first note-on as a reset rather than -120 dB. Also warn when a voice's mean velocity_eff falls below about 10 while its input velocities are much higher, or when normalise_gain_db exceeds +20 dB. State the CC1 convention in the README next to the 'any MIDI' claim.

defects.issue: The hall is about 9 dB wetter on piano material than the documentation and render report say. The IR is scaled to unit energy, so '--wet-db -4 = hall energy relative to the dry piano' and 'C80 of about +8 dB' only hold for a white impulse. The IR's energy sits at 63-1000 Hz, where the piano's energy is.
defects.evidence: qa/round2/results/hall.json. On the demo at the default -4 dB: hall-to-dry energy is +5.2 dB broadband (+6.7/+6.9/+4.7/+4.8/+4.7 dB at 63/125/250/500/1000 Hz). Clarity (C80) measured on the program is +2.1 dB, against the report's c80_db 8.4. Per-band IR C80 with the dry path added: +3.4/+2.2/+1.2/+0.7/+2.0 dB at 63-1000 Hz. The documented behaviour (hall -3.8 dB, C80 +7.5) actually needs --wet-db -13. -10 gives hall -0.8 dB, C80 +5.3; -7 gives +2.2 dB, +3.5. Cost to articulation (qa/round2/results/demo_clarity.json): median onset contrast from no reverb to default drops alto 25.4->22.1, tenor 18.3->15.4, pedal 14.5->10.6 dB. Pedal notes with less than 3 dB contrast go from 7 to 13 of 86. Bass 16ths at quarter=144 drop from 6.5 to 4.8 dB median (fast16). Most notes remain clearly articulated.
defects.fix: Compute c80_db in the render report on the program: dry sum plus the first 80 ms of wet, against the rest, which is what an_hall.program() does. Either calibrate --wet-db against a piano long-term spectrum rather than a white impulse, or document that -4 means the hall is about +5 dB over the dry piano on this material. Choose the default on that basis: -8 to -10 gives program C80 of +3.5 to +5.3 dB. Update README line 54 and the render_piano.py docstring.

defects.issue: The reverb tail is cut in the bass. The Detmold source IR is only 1.5 s long, but the hall's low-frequency T20 is 1.8-2.2 s. make_ir.py's 150 ms end fade therefore removes the bass tail about 40 dB down. This is inaudible in the demo, whose last chord has decayed to -38 dB before key-up. It is audible after an ff staccato ending or a general pause.
defects.evidence: qa/round2/results/tail_truncation.json. Probe: ff chord (C2 to C4, velocity 120, 0.4 s), default render. The 63 Hz band decays at -20.8 dB/s until 1.3 s after key-up, then at -142.6 dB/s from -40.8 dB relative to its peak. The 125 Hz band goes from -22.0 to -141.6 dB/s, starting at -45.3 dB. Broadband level falls from -49.5 to -64.6 dB between 1.30 and 1.40 s after key-up. The IR's band level where the fade starts (1.29 s): -40.2 dB at 63 Hz, -38.5 dB at 125 Hz. IR T20: 2.19 s at 63 Hz, 1.78 s at 125 Hz. The source Omni/S1R163.wav is 1.5 s.
defects.fix: In make_ir.py, extend the late tail per octave band with exponentially decaying noise matched to the measured T20 and to the level and inter-channel correlation of the last 200 ms, out to at least 3 s. Fade only once the tail is below -80 dB. Record the extension in the IR JSON, and re-check with a staccato ff chord.

defects.issue: Loudness rises smoothly with velocity, but brightness jumps at the sample-layer boundaries. There are no velocity crossfades, and layer 3 covers only velocities 35-36.
defects.evidence: qa/round2/results/velsweep.json (velocity 1-127 in steps of 2). The level is monotonic everywhere: largest step 1.6 dB per 2 velocities, no reversals, correlation 0.98. The HF ratio (share of energy above 2 kHz) is flat inside each layer but jumps at boundaries: C2 +7.2 dB at v35 and +7.3 dB at v37 while level moves 1.1 and 0.8 dB; C4 +5.0 and +4.9 dB; C6 +5.0 dB at v51 and +4.8 dB at v65. Through the chain (dyn2 hairpin, per beat) the HF ratio runs -33.8, -34.0, -27.4, -27.4, -23.1 dB across the first five beats while level moves 0.6-3.3 dB per beat.
defects.fix: Add xfin_lovel/xfin_hivel and xfout_lovel/xfout_hivel crossfades of about 4-8 velocities between adjacent layers in make_sfz.py, at least for layers 1-6. Alternatively, widen or merge the 2-velocity layers (v35-36, v44-46). Re-measure with an_velsweep.py.

defects.issue: Damper release noises sound 75-190 ms after key-up instead of at key-up. The rel*.flac samples play with their recorded pre-roll; unlike the note samples, they have no offset= trim.
defects.evidence: qa/round2 iso analysis: the high-frequency event after key-up has a median delay of 110 ms (range 75-190 ms) across A0-E6. Sample pre-roll: rel1 23 ms to -40 dB and 148 ms to -20 dB; rel20 46/109 ms; rel40 39/49 ms. In the demo, all 12 apparent onsets later than 20 ms at C2 and above are this noise: each falls 38-83 ms after the same voice's previous key-up (qa/round2/results/chain_demo_j4.json, note_on_late_onsets).
defects.fix: In make_sfz.py, give each trigger=release region an offset= at its -40 dB onset point, as is already done for the note samples. Optionally suppress rel* while CC64 is down (sustain_sw or on_locc64 gating), since lifting a key under the pedal makes no damper noise.

defects.issue: Two tracks with the same name are silently merged into one voice. The docstring says every (track, channel) pair holding notes becomes a voice.
defects.evidence: odd_names probe: two tracks both named 'soprano' (notes 72 and 76) render as one stem 'soprano' with 2 notes; the report lists voices [soprano, track3]. The shared stem also shares the CC7 fader and --transpose.
defects.fix: In load_midi, suffix duplicate track names ('soprano', 'soprano.2') or print a warning, and document the behaviour.

defects.issue: Small robustness and documentation gaps: (a) setup_piano.sh rebuilds the hall IR only if it is missing or with --force; unlike the SFZ it records no generator hash, so an edited make_ir.py goes unnoticed. (b) render_piano.py's fallback marks in perform_vel_map (ppp 12, pp 29, mp 64) differ from the calibration's suggested_velocities (13, 30, 63). (c) The stretch tuning is not documented, yet it sets the 16-foot pedal line clearly below the other voices.
defects.evidence: qa/round2/results/setup_idempotency.json: today the regenerated IR matches the installed one exactly (max difference 0.0). (b) render_piano.py line 358. (c) Isolated keys, energy-weighted partials 1-6: A0 -22.8, C1 -18.2, F#1 -12.5, C3 -2.7, C4 about -1, F5 +4.5, C6 +8.9, C8 +39 cents. In the demo, the pedal at --transpose -12 sits at a median -10.8 cents (p5 -15.8), while alto, soprano and tenor medians are +0.9, +2.4 and -1.6.
defects.fix: (a) Write make_ir.py's sha256 into the IR JSON and check it in setup, as is done for the SFZ. (b) Use the calibration values as the fallback. (c) Add the stretch curve (A0 about -23, C4 0, C8 +39 cents) to the README Limits section.

qa.measurements:
Environment: load average about 800 on 16 cores, disk 99% full. Renders were run serially except where stated. My scripts and results are committed under /Users/biobook/Music/llm-music/fugue-jp/ricercar/audio/piano/qa/round2/ (commits 4a8234f through f7fb81e; no renderer code was touched). No audio was committed.

END-TO-END CHAIN, run exactly as documented: perform.py fugue.ly with plans/fugue_jp.plan.json and --target piano, then render_piano.py with --transpose pedal=-12 and --jobs 4.
- The regenerated MIDI is byte-identical to out/fugue_jp.mid.
- Against LilyPond's own MIDI of fugue.ly: 647/647 notes matched by pitch and onset. perform.py has 648; the extra note is a soprano/alto unison that LilyPond writes once.
- Renderer: 648 input notes, 647 sent to sfizz, plus 1 merged unison (as documented). 0 missing. Stem MIDI timing error max 0.026 ms. Velocities match the perform-to-calibration map (the one mismatch is the merged unison's stronger velocity).
- sfizz onsets, C2 and above: median 1.8 ms, p95 6 ms. Isolated keys A0-C8 at velocity 80: 2-10 ms to within 20 dB of peak.
- Release on key lift: iso, 150-250 ms after key-up, A0-E2 -30.1 dB and F2-E6 -27.8 dB (F6-C8 ring on, -4.3 dB). Demo rests: -25.5 to -35.5 dB.
- No stuck notes: every stem falls more than 60 dB below its peak within 0.14-0.19 s of the last key-up.
- Truncation: the first render plus 3 concurrent --jobs 4 renders (12 sfizz instances) at load about 800 gave 0 truncations, 0 re-renders, and stems bit-identical across runs.

PITCH:
- Velocity layers of one key agree within 1 cent (C2 -5.3 to -4.4, C4 -2.4 to -2.0, C6 +8.8 to +9.7 cents).
- The stretch curve is smooth; the largest step between neighbouring keys is about 2 cents (energy-weighted).
- Demo medians against equal temperament, partial 1: alto +0.9 (p5 -3.3, p95 +3.1), soprano +2.4 (+1.2 to +4.9), tenor -1.6 (-5.5 to +2.8).
- Pedal -10.8 cents: this is the piano's stretch at C1-A#1 (iso gives -9 to -18 there).
- The octave checks confirm that --transpose pedal=-12 sounds an octave lower.

- After gain-matching pp to ff, pp is -4.1/-15.3/-23.6/-29.8 dB at 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz. A pure gain change would leave every band at 0.
- Hairpin pp-ff-pp over repeated notes: 22.2 dB level span, 16.0 dB HF span, correlation with the plan 0.993 (HF 0.89), 0 steps against the ramp, largest step 3.3 dB per beat (perform.py's metric accents).
- Voicing: the alto as subject moves from -0.3 to +3.4 dB against the other voices (+3.7 dB) and from 532 to 540 Hz centroid.
